title: Systems of Linear Equations
description: Substitution, elimination and Gaussian elimination, solvability.
html:
📊 Systems of Linear Equations

1. Meaning

Two equations with two unknowns describe two lines. Possible solution sets: exactly one point, empty (parallel) or infinitely many (identical). Never exactly two.

$$\begin{cases} x + y = 3 \\ x - y = 1 \end{cases} \Rightarrow (x, y) = (2, 1)$$

2. Solution methods

Substitution / equating

Solve one equation for a variable and substitute into the other.

Elimination

Scale the equations so that one variable cancels when adding. Check in both equations.

Special cases

  • $0 = c$ with $c \neq 0$: no solution
  • $0 = 0$: infinitely many solutions (free parameter)

3. Gaussian elimination

Set up the augmented matrix, use row operations (swap rows, multiply by $\lambda \neq 0$, add a multiple) to reach echelon form, solve from the bottom up.

$$\left(\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 & 2 \end{array}\right) \to \cdots \to (x, y, z) = (1, 2, 3)$$

4. Solvability

  • Row $(0\ 0\ 0 \mid c)$, $c \neq 0$: unsolvable
  • Every variable has a pivot: exactly one solution
  • Variable without a pivot: infinitely many solutions. Number of parameters = unknowns $-$ pivots

With parameters, look for the critical value (e.g. where a pivot vanishes) and examine this case separately.
